dollar.source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, CPI-U not seasonally adjusted (CPIAUCNS), annual averages; today = 2026-08 monthly index.

interest.source: OMB Historical Tables FY2027, Table 3.1 (outlays by function) and Table 2.1 (individual income tax receipts); IRS Statistics of Income returns filed. Fiscal years. Per taxpayer = outlay ÷ individual returns filed (160,602,107 returns, latest IRS tax year 2023).

holders.source: U.S. Treasury via FRED: debt held by the public (FYGFDPUN), foreign holders (FDHBFIN); Federal Reserve holdings (FDHBFRBN). Annual averages of quarterly data.

plumbing.source: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, H.4.1, via FRED (RRPONTSYD, WRESBAL, WLCFLPCL, H41RESPPALDKNWW, TREAST). Lines are annual averages; dots mark each facility's single highest weekly/daily reading (the spikes annual averages hide).

gold.russia_note: Russia's IMF data stop in mid-2024.
gold.wgc_note: IMF counts only purchases central banks report. The World Gold Council estimates over 1,000 t/yr in 2022–24 including unreported buying.
gold.citation: Source: International Monetary Fund, International Financial Statistics (accessed via DBnomics); tonnes and net flows are our calculation.
gold.source: U.S. holdings: U.S. Treasury Fiscal Data, Status Report of U.S. Government Gold Reserve (2026-08-31), market value at the World Bank Pink Sheet gold price. World and country flows: IMF IFS official reserve gold (RAFAGOLDV_OZT), end-year holdings; net purchases = change in holdings; 1 t = 32,150.75 oz.
